mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS < 0.5% but 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE 3-month change > 0.3pp but 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages signals robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both above 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: HOUST and RSAFS both above 12-month moving averages but 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes (defined by GDP growth exceeding 2.5% annualized and unemployment rate below 5%), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns due to overvaluation and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth > 2.5% annualized and UNRATE < 5% but 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average signals strong supply chain activity, correlating with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO > 12-month moving average but 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPIAUCSL value exceeding 230.5 signals persistent inflation, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 230.5 but 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous payroll employment growth exceeding 0.5% monthly and unemployment rate below 4.5% signals a strong labor market, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly and UNRATE < 4.5% but 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a demand contraction regime (defined by housing starts and retail sales both below their 12-month moving averages), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns due to reduced consumer spending, leading to negative 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both below 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: HOUST and RSAFS both below 12-month moving averages but 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances.
